claims.statement: The release-please-managed manifest records independent current release baselines: libs/deepagents 0.7.25, libs/acp 0.0.13, libs/code 0.1.84, libs/talon 0.0.9, daytona 0.0.8, modal 0.0.6, runloop 0.0.7, vercel 0.0.2, and quickjs 0.3.9.

The current deepagents-code source version is 0.1.84 in both project metadata and its release-please-managed version marker, its changelog records that release, and its exact deepagents dependency pin is 0.7.24.

Development is package-scoped: the repository guide requires uv rather than pip, Poetry, or Conda, identifies each package Makefile as the command authority, and directs contributors to use uv sync in the package they change.

The Deep Agents and Code Makefiles set UV_FROZEN=true; their unit-test targets run the test group with parallel pytest, non-Unix sockets disabled and Unix sockets allowed, while their lint targets verify Ruff formatting and run ty.

Code's make check is a local CI-parity gate that runs lint, import checks, and tests, then checks extras synchronization, version-marker equality, and uv.lock freshness; only exit status 1 from its SDK-pin check is advisory.

Code resolves deepagents, deepagents-acp, and its listed partner integrations through editable sibling paths in tool.uv.sources, allowing local consumer development without publishing those distributions.

The aggregate libs Makefile discovers library/partner Makefiles and example manifests, stops fan-out recipes on failure, resolves ACP locks with Python 3.14 and all other discovered locks with Python 3.12, and provides lock, lock-check, and lock-bump targets.

The dependency-minimums updater raises only >= and ~= floors for in-scope PyPI-resolved langchain, langgraph, langsmith, and deepagents requirements; it preserves upper bounds, extras, and markers, skips exact pins and already-higher floors, and fails rather than silently treating unresolved PyPI metadata or invalid requested narrowing as current.

When dependency floors change, the updater computes the transitive reverse closure of local tool.uv.sources consumers because their locks embed producer requirements; skip-dependent-locks deliberately returns only directly changed package locks.

The dependency-minimums workflow runs daily at 09:00 UTC or manually, invokes the updater, regenerates each reported directory=Python lock specification, and creates or refreshes a generated dependency PR only when edits occurred.

Release-please is configured for nine separately drafted Python release PRs with per-package changelogs and extra version files, uses release(component): version titles and pre-1.0 bump behavior, and delegates GitHub release creation to release.yml.

Release-please blocks ordinary empty commits because component attribution comes from changed paths and a pathless commit can otherwise fan out to every package; after a release-PR merge it detects a release only when both a matching release(component): version title and that component's CHANGELOG.md change are present.

The curated-release-notes check validates only release-please release branches, creates a refreshed check on the actual release PR head for comment/manual runs, and its always finalizer turns an interrupted in-progress refresh check into failure rather than leaving it pending.

The release workflow maps the package to a working directory, resolves an exact release SHA, validates normal-release source version consistency, refuses an already-published or unverifiable PyPI version, publishes artifacts to TestPyPI after build and pre-release checks, and uses trusted publishing for that step.
Release-note generation is deliberately non-blocking: a failure does not prevent publishing or creating the GitHub release, so an otherwise successful release can have an empty release body.

Current package manifests define distinct runtime Python and dependency-floor contracts: ACP and QuickJS require Python 3.11 or newer, Code and Talon require Python 3.12 or newer, and Deep Agents supports Python 3.11 or newer below Python 4; their listed LangChain, LangGraph, LangSmith, and Deep Agents requirements carry package-specific floors and bounds.

The curated-notes helper trusts only an open same-repository release-please branch targeting main, derives the component's package and changelog path from the release-please configuration, and requires the release title's component to agree with the branch component before treating a PR as a release target.

For a successful release, release.yml creates the GitHub release tag from the resolved release SHA and transitions the associated release PR from pending to tagged, preventing later release-please maintenance from treating the package as half-published.
After publishing deepagents successfully, the release workflow dispatches the separate Code SDK-pin bump workflow as a non-blocking post-publish convenience.

The updater preserves compatible-release ceilings by rendering a raised ~= floor with the original number of release components, plans all manifest changes before writing them, and rejects a planned rewrite that would exclude a PyPI version allowed by the original range.

Current core compatibility floors are langchain>=1.4.5,<2.0.0 for Deep Agents, Code, Talon, and QuickJS; Deep Agents, Talon, and QuickJS require langchain-core>=1.6.10,<2.0.0 where declared, while Talon and QuickJS require langgraph>=1.2.15,<2.0.0.

CI invokes the reusable lockfile workflow on pull requests, pushes to main, and merge groups; that workflow runs the lockfile checker, which resolves ACP checks with Python 3.14 and all other package checks with Python 3.12.
